solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Male animal that may be made fast?

definitions.meaning: the male of deer, rabbits and hares
a quick, easily earned dollar is a 'fast ...', ... being slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A riddle about which male creature might be speeded up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading turns on the phrase 'make a fast buck', meaning to earn money quickly, with buck as American slang for a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: Stags, rams and other male deer or rabbits are called bucks.

clue.text: Little in the way of support for such spiteful talk!

indicators.note: the small piece is placed in the word for support, getting in its way

parts.note: backing is support
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: An exclamation at gossip that offers almost no backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark hints at the &lit flavour: backbiters give little support. 'in the way of' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbiting is malicious talk about someone behind their back.

clue.text: Farewell from guerrilla leader to north of European port

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits above, north of, what follows

parts.note: Che Guevara was a Latin American guerrilla leader
Rio de Janeiro, Rio for short, is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A rebel commander bids goodbye from a European harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye.

clue.text: Trauma-resistant old academic goes about with untidy mass of hair

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick tousled mop

indicators.note: the academic's title wraps around the next piece, going about it

parts.note: PROF is short for professor

explanation.surface: An elderly professor with wild hair is somehow immune to trauma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is just a link joining the hair to the academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shockproof withstands jolts and impacts, so it resists trauma.

clue.text: Flowering shrub the rain so damaged

indicators.note: damage knocks the letters out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden plant battered by heavy rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges THE, RAIN and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hortensia is a name for the common mophead hydrangea, a bush grown for its blooms.

clue.text: Old measure of copper coin?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Asking how a historical coin's worth was reckoned.
explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The cubit is an ancient length unit, forearm length from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: Advance idea from papa about beginning of pregnancy

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
re means about or concerning
conception is the moment a pregnancy starts

explanation.surface: A father's notion about his partner's pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A preconception is an opinion formed in advance, before the facts are known.

clue.text: Like a complex king's gem worn by English princess?

indicators.note: the gem goes around the next pieces, as jewellery is worn around a person

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A royal gem worn by an English princess, with a hint of a complicated king.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'complex' is the Oedipus complex, named after the king of Thebes in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipal relates to the Oedipus complex, named after the mythical Theban king.

clue.text: Model's criminal record

definitions.meaning: a shape or pattern to copy
British slang for a record of past convictions

explanation.surface: A fashion model turns out to have a police record.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Form means both a pattern or model and, in British slang, a criminal history.

clue.text: Less expensive-sounding young bird?

indicators.note: signals that the word for less expensive is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cheaper means costing less

explanation.surface: A bargain fledgling, cheaper than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeper is a young game bird such as a partridge or grouse, named for its call; the question mark flags the playful sense.

clue.text: Game to approve the plot?

parts.note: to pass is to approve, as a law is passed
a parcel is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A council game: approving a planning application.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a British children's party game where a wrapped prize is handed round until the music stops.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a party game in which a layered parcel is unwrapped when the music stops.

clue.text: Kitchen appliance ultimately useful in drinking-spree

indicators.note: the final letter is placed in the word for a binge

parts.note: a bender is a bout of heavy drinking

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of useful

explanation.surface: A handy kitchen gadget proves useful during a binge, perhaps for cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes L from useful; 'in' puts it inside BENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is the electric jug used for liquidising food.

clue.text: Swift action is needed to make this course possible

definitions.text: Swift action is needed to make this course possible

parts.words: Swift action is needed to make this course possible
parts.note: the swift is a bird whose saliva nests are the key ingredient of a Chinese delicacy served as a course

explanation.surface: Quick work is needed to get this dish to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift action' seems to mean haste; it is the swiftlet bird building its edible nest.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese soup is made from the nests swiftlets build from saliva, served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Son leaves Waugh's house, skirting key part of fortification

indicators.note: the shortened house runs round the key, skirting it
the son departs, so his letter is removed

parts.note: Brideshead is the country house in Evelyn Waugh's novel Brideshead Revisited
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A son moves out of a novelist's mansion, avoiding a vital part of its defences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops S from BRIDESHEAD; 'skirting' puts G inside. 'key' looks like an adjective with 'part' but is the musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a fortified position at the end of a bridge facing the enemy.

clue.text: Political extremist sheltering union leader? Something fishy here

indicators.note: the extremist encloses the next letter, giving it shelter

parts.note: TROT is short for Trotskyist, a far-left radical

indicators.note: the leader of union is its first letter

explanation.surface: A radical harbours a trade union boss, and something smells fishy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes U from union; 'sheltering' puts it inside TROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish, so it is literally something fishy.

clue.text: Broadcast our clubs initially adjudged beneath the viewers

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters are scattered
initially points to the first letter of adjudged

explanation.surface: A sports report on how a team's clubs were first judged on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives A from adjudged; 'Broadcast' shuffles OUR, CLUBS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Subocular is an anatomical term for lying below the eyes, which are the viewers.

clue.text: Teacher's policy primarily delivered cover in retirement

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teacher's degree; with 's it gives BEDS

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of policy

parts.note: read means delivered aloud, as a speech is read

explanation.surface: A retiring teacher's policy announcement offered cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes P from policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the top cover on a bed, used when one retires for the night.

clue.text: Shark, unusually ferocious, gobbling up one's nanny

parts.note: the nurse shark is a species of shark

indicators.note: the word for ferocious swallows the next letter

parts.note: mad, as of a dog, means abnormally wild and savage
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A savage shark devours someone's nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal but just intensifies ferocious; 'gobbling up' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children, the job of a nanny.

clue.text: Soldiers composed unfinished Mass, one for the departed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is cut off, leaving it incomplete

parts.note: composed means calm or quiet
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Troops wrote a partial Mass to honour the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the end of QUIET, leaving QUIE. 'composed' and 'Mass' suggest music.
explanation.definitionFit: A requiem is a Mass or composition for the souls of the dead.

clue.text: Patrolled, with due deference to duke

parts.note: pace is the Latin-derived word meaning with respect to someone who might disagree

explanation.surface: A guard walked the rounds, mindful of the duke's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry who paced walked back and forth on watch, as one does on patrol.

clue.text: Room in which daily is invested with award

indicators.note: the cleaner is filled with the honour, like a robe put on

parts.note: a daily or char is a British term for a cleaning woman
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: The room where a cleaning lady receives her honour.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a cleaner who comes in each day; 'is invested with' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a bedroom or formal hall.

clue.text: Greatly increase output of ducal art and equip …

indicators.note: the letters are what the words produce when reworked, their output

explanation.surface: An instruction to multiply production of a duke's art and kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'output of' rearranges DUCAL, ART and EQUIP; 'and' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To quadruplicate is to multiply by four, a large increase.

clue.text: Relax about start of Italian exam

indicators.note: the word for relax goes about the letter from Italian

parts.note: to rest is to relax

indicators.note: the start of Italian is its first letter

explanation.surface: Take a break before an Italian test begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives I; 'about' puts REST around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an exam taken again after failing it.

clue.text: Rising at university, inspired by outstanding work

indicators.note: the outstanding piece breathes in the other, holding it inside

parts.note: OS is outsize, an abbreviation for very large

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the words are read from the bottom up

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student rising at university, inspired by an outstanding piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses in a down clue; 'inspired by' signals the insertion. Being 'up' at university is a British idiom for studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition.

clue.text: … royals of note overwhelmed by costs

indicators.note: the note is swamped by the word for costs, which surrounds it

parts.note: prices are costs

explanation.surface: Following on, famous royals buried under their expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the clue before; it plays no part in the wordplay. 'overwhelmed by' puts N inside PRICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Princes are the sons of monarchs, members of a royal family.

clue.text: King George leaves French city, receiving knight to elevate

indicators.note: the shortened city takes in the knight
the king departs, so his letters are removed from the city

parts.note: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A king quits a French city and takes a knight with him to promote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops GR from GRENOBLE to give ENOBLE; 'receiving' inserts N.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, lifting their rank.

clue.text: Comparison limits one due for development

indicators.note: the letters are to be developed into a new form

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A comparison caps one person due for growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for development' rearranges LIMITS, I and DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Similitude is likeness, and a simile or comparison expresses it.

clue.text: Brought up money for speaker?

indicators.note: the word for money is as a speaker would say it, not as it is written

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A question of whether cash was raised for a public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means raised or reared, as a child is brought up.
